svg.title: Relative-commutant repairs lose the flip or commutation
svg.desc: Exact Section5B proof. One-sided closure replaces B by C, yielding mutual relative commutants but ambient commutants of different finiteness. Two-sided closure replaces both by C and D, retaining the internal flip and joint generation, but two reduced word outputs prove noncommutation. The second failure persists for the full stabilized factor.

g.text: Full commutants do not repair the generating pair.
Exact calculations · Γ = F(a₀,a₁,...) · π(a₀) = e, π(aₙ₊₁) = bₙ
C = A′ ∩ E = RΓ ⊗̄ RΔ · D = B′ ∩ E = JCJ
Use the regular commutation proof for Γ × Δ, not a tensor-intersection shortcut.
B ⊊ C and A ⊊ D · Lemma 5B.1
Close one side: A and C.
C′ ∩ E = A · A ∨ C = E
Ambient A′ = RΓ ⊗̄ B(ℓ²(Δ))
contains a nonunitary isometry.
Ambient C′ = LΓ ⊗̄ LΔ has a finite trace.
No spatial unitary exchanges this pair.
LΓ, LΔ denote left regular algebras · Proposition 5B.2
Close both sides: C and D.
JCJ = D · C ∨ D = E
C ∩ D = ℂ1
Z = 1 ⊗ ρb₀ ∈ C · Y = JZJ ∈ D
ZY ≠ YZ · exact basis witness below.
Internal flip survives · Proposition 5B.3
ξ = δa₂ ⊗ δe · π(a₂) = b₁ · ‖ξ‖ = 1
ZYξ = δa₂ ⊗ δ(b₁⁻¹ b₀⁻¹ b₁ b₀⁻¹)
YZξ = δa₂ ⊗ δ(b₀⁻¹ b₁⁻¹ b₀⁻¹ b₁)
Reduced words start differently: the two basis vectors are orthogonal.
Whole-factor relative commutants: Ĉ = P′ ∩ M̃; D̂ = Q′ ∩ M̃.
SĈS = D̂ · Ĉ ∨ D̂ = M̃ · Ĉ ∩ D̂ = ℂ1
Identity tensors of Z and Y still have commutator norm at least √2.
Both closures fail to commute · Corollary 5B.4 · preserved on transport to M₀.
Excluded: these relative-commutant repair operations for the displayed pair.
Other-pair existence remains open · Connes, Corollary 11, author PDF 44–45.
